steps.hint: Super + - and Super + = move the split left or right. Whichever edge has room will move; try both.
steps.why: Resizing is relative: tap a few times to get the width you want.

steps.hint: Add Shift: Super + Shift + - / =. If the windows are side by side, press Super + J first so they stack and height can change.
steps.why: Shift = the other axis. Same pattern as before.

steps.hint: Super + Alt + Home remembers this window's width. Nothing visible happens yet.
steps.why: Save now, restore later — handy for a terminal you keep at one size.

steps.say: Change the width, then restore it.
steps.hint: Change the width first (Super + - / =), then Super + Home snaps it back to the saved width.
steps.why: Restore is the payoff of the previous step.

steps.hint: Super + O floats the window and pins it above every workspace.
steps.why: Pop-out is for a reference window you want on top of everything.
